sn7.11:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Magadhans on the Southern Hill near the brahmin village Ekanālā.
sn7.11:1.3: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja had about five hundred ploughs yoked up during the sowing season.
sn7.11:1.4: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, approached the place where the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja was working.
sn7.11:2.1: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja’s food distribution was proceeding.
sn7.11:2.2: Then the Fortunate One approached the food distribution, and after approaching he stood on one side.
sn7.11:2.3: The brahmin Kasībhāradvāja saw the Fortunate One standing for alms,
sn7.11:2.4: and after seeing him he said this to the Fortunate One:
sn7.11:2.5: “Ascetic, I plough and I sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.
sn7.11:2.6: You also, ascetic, should plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing you can eat.”
sn7.11:2.7: “Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.”
sn7.11:2.8: “But we do not see the reverend Gotama’s yoke or plough or ploughshare or goad or oxen, but still the reverend Gotama said this:
sn7.11:2.9: ‘Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.’ ”
sn7.11:2.10: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
sn7.11:3.1: “You claim that you are a ploughman,
sn7.11:3.2: but we do not see your ploughing.
sn7.11:3.3: Please tell us about ploughing when asked
sn7.11:3.4: so that we may know your ploughing.”
sn7.11:4.2: wisdom is my yoke and plough,
sn7.11:4.3: conscience the pole, mind is the strap,
sn7.11:4.4: mindfulness is my ploughshare and goad.
sn7.11:5.4: temperance the setting free (of the yoke).
sn7.11:6.4: to that place where, having gone, one does not grieve.
sn7.11:7.1: Thus this ploughing has been ploughed
sn7.11:7.2: that produces the fruit of the deathless,
sn7.11:7.4: one is set free from all suffering.”
sn7.11:8.2: the reverend one is a ploughman,
sn7.11:8.3: for the reverend Gotama ploughs the ploughing which has the deathless as fruit.”
sn7.11:9.1: “I will not eat what is gained through chanting verses,
sn7.11:9.2: that is not the Dhamma, brahmin, of those who see,
sn7.11:9.3: Buddhas reject what is gained through chanting verses,
sn7.11:9.4: while Dhamma lasts, brahmin, this is their way of life.
sn7.11:10.1: Another great sage, who is fully adept,
sn7.11:10.2: pollutant-free, at peace regarding worry (about wrong-doing),
sn7.11:10.3: attend to with food and drink,
sn7.11:10.4: for that is the field for those who look for merit.”
